label: Aquinas on willing a creature's esse and directing creatures to ends
summary: ST I q.20 a.2 co. derives willing a creature's esse to it on the basis of q.19 a.4's will as cause. Its ad 3 orders irrational creatures to rational creatures and God under quasi-desire. That reply does not assert the exclusive denial of willing a creature's esse to it, nor specify the typed esse-indexed ordering of 7f6a2e91 as a separate thesis. ST I q.22 aa.1–2 puts every creature, including each individual insofar as it participates in being, under the ordering of the universal first cause, with providence in intellect and presupposing a willed end. The chosen generic causation relations leave acting through will open in both routes.
blocker: Make causation through will explicit in applications of the two claims. For love, preserve the difference between a good willed to a creature and that creature being ordered to another. For providence, preserve the distinction between the plan and execution.
